title: CSO: Refining Robotic Policies via Skill Distribution Alignment and Skill-Grained Optimization
claim: A two-stage post-training procedure first aligns the skill prior with successful trajectories, then refines it with skill-level group RL.
layout: 2 stacked stages split by dashed line, left-to-right, shared Skill Prior block
description: A wide diagram showing a two-stage post-training pipeline for a robot policy. At left, a dashed box labelled Env State holds an RGB image, a robot arm icon for proprioception, and a text instruction ("open the top drawer"). These feed three grey encoders (image, state, text) inside a blue dashed region. The encoders are fused into coloured tokens that enter a tall blue Skill Prior block. A dashed horizontal line splits the figure into Stage 1 R-SFT (top) and Stage 2 SPO (bottom). In Stage 1, skill sequences are paired with observations as trajectories. Green check and red cross marks route successful trajectories into a Replay Buffer, with an arrow back for supervised fine-tuning. In Stage 2, trajectories are collected into a Group with check/cross outcomes and passed to an SPO box. A feedback arrow returns to the Skill Prior as a skill-level RL update. Pastel colours code the tokens.
caption: The architecture and data flow of our proposed CSO framework. Stage 1 (R-SFT): The initial policy is executed to collect trajectories, and successful trajectories are stored in a replay buffer. The observation-to-skill policy is then fine-tuned on this curated dataset using a supervised objective; the action tokenizer and decoder remain fixed. Stage 2 (SPO): With the encoders now frozen, the policy collects groups of trajectories. The SPO algorithm then updates the skill prior with a skill-level policy gradient based on terminal group-relative advantages.
abstract: Discretizing continuous actions into discrete skills using methods like VQ-VAE has emerged as a powerful paradigm for robotic manipulation. However, quantization errors yield a suboptimal distribution for the skill prior, degrading its performance. While reinforcement learning offers a path for refinement, its direct application faces unstable encoder updates and a granularity dilemma in importance sampling. To address these challenges, we introduce Cascaded Skills Optimization (CSO), a two-stage post-training framework. First, Rejection-Sampling Supervised Fine-tuning aligns the model's observation-to-skill mapping with the distribution of successful online trajectories via supervised fine-tuning. Second, with the observation encoder frozen, Skills Policy Optimization computes an independent, clipped importance ratio for each complete skill, enabling stable and efficient updates. With a lightweight QueST-style policy, CSO raises overall LIBERO success from 80.1% to 97.5%, improves performance on RoboTwin2.0, and achieves 61.0% success across five physical single-arm tasks. Additional comparisons with FAST, discrete BEAST, and fixed-buffer IQL further validate the effectiveness of our two-stage post-training strategy.
